newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Iraqi disarmament official to leave his post.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Iraqi disarmament official to leave his post.

text.p: Rolf Ekeus, the executive chairman of the U.N. commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament, was expected to leave his post by the end of the year to become Sweden's ambassador to Washington, diplomatic sources said on Friday.

Ekeus' name was submitted to the State Department earlier this week by the Swedish government for approval. U.S. officials were reported to have been upset by leaks of the news before Washington had given its official agreement.
The appointment to replace Ambassador Henrik Liljegren was not expected to take place before the end of the summer.
The Stockholm newspaper Dagens Nyheter reported the news early on Friday but Swedish envoys would not comment on the report, which cited unidentified diplomats.

One possible candidate to replace Ekeus was Emilio Cardenas, Argentina's former ambassador to the United Nations, who has returned to the private sector in Buenos Aires. He was interviewed for the post in mid-January but diplomats said several other candidates would be considered.
His highly regarded deputy, Charles Duelfer, was an unlikely successor because he is an American.
Ekeus, 62, over the past year has said he considered leaving the U.N. post several times but had been persuaded to stay a bit longer.

He is head of the U.N. Speciai Commission in charge of ridding Iraq of weapons of mass destruction -- including nuclear warheads, biological and chemical arms and ballistic missiles. Sanctions against Iraq, imposed after it invaded Kuwait in 1990, cannot be lifted until Ekeus is satisfied he has accounted for all the dangerous weapons.
Ekeus, on instructions from the Security Council, organised the commission in April 1991. It was considered one of the most efficient in the United Nations.
He has frequently accused Iraq of misleading his weapons inspectors and in turn has been castigated by Baghdad officials and media for being a front for the United States.
